Marketplace Category Remediation

Identified and resolved duplicate category metadata across hundreds of marketplace connectors using AI-assisted code analysis and bulk automation.

Data QualityAI-Assisted AnalysisMarketplaceGitHub Automation

Problem

The product's Content Library displayed duplicate and inconsistent category names in the filter panel. For example:

  • "SIEM & Log Management" and "SIEM and Log Management" appeared as separate categories
  • "Endpoint Security & Management" and "Endpoint Security and Management" coexisted
  • "Identity & Access Management" and "Identity Management" showed as distinct entries

This created a confusing user experience where customers could not reliably filter connectors by category, and the marketplace appeared unpolished.

My Role

I owned the investigation, root cause analysis, remediation plan, stakeholder communication, and execution of the fix across all affected connector repositories.

What I Did

  1. Investigated the root cause by using AI-assisted code analysis to trace how categories flow from connector metadata through the SDK to the marketplace UI. Identified that categories are stored as keywords in each connector's connector.yaml file, and the canonical category list was defined in the SDK but not enforced
  2. Mapped the discrepancies between the canonical category list (in the SDK) and actual connector metadata across the connector organization. Found that connectors created at different times used inconsistent naming (ampersands vs. spelled-out "and", abbreviations vs. full names)
  3. Built a remediation script that:
    • Iterated across all connector repositories
    • Read each connector's connector.yaml
    • Mapped old/incorrect category names to canonical versions
    • Created pull requests with the corrected metadata
  4. Managed the republishing workflow by determining that fixing the YAML alone was insufficient; connectors needed to be republished for the marketplace to reflect the corrected categories
  5. Communicated the plan and progress to my manager with clear write-ups of the problem scope, approach, and status at each stage

Constraints

  • Hundreds of separate repositories to update (one per connector)
  • GitHub API rate limits restricted bulk operations
  • Republishing required marketplace admin credentials and coordination with the team
  • Some connectors required manual category assignment because their original categories did not map cleanly to the canonical list

Outcomes

Customer Impact

  • Eliminated duplicate categories from the Content Library filter panel
  • Improved connector discoverability for customers browsing by category
  • Cleaned up the marketplace's professional appearance

Process Impact

  • Established a validated category mapping that prevents future drift
  • Demonstrated a repeatable pattern for bulk metadata remediation across large connector catalogs
  • Identified that the SDK's category enum was outdated and needed alignment with the canonical list

AI-Assisted Workflow

This project used AI-assisted code analysis (Cursor) throughout:

  • Root cause tracing: AI helped navigate the SDK codebase to locate where categories are defined, validated, and consumed
  • Impact assessment: AI helped enumerate all connector repositories using wrong category names and classify the discrepancies
  • Script generation: AI assisted in building the bulk remediation and PR-creation scripts
  • Stakeholder communication: AI helped draft clear, non-technical write-ups for manager communication

Lessons Learned

  • Data quality problems in marketplaces are often invisible until a customer (or team member) notices the filter panel; proactive auditing is worthwhile
  • Fixing metadata at the source is always the right approach, even when it means updating hundreds of repositories instead of patching the UI
  • AI-assisted code analysis dramatically accelerated the investigation; tracing category flow through SDK source code would have taken days manually
